consumer: The frontend map renderer that paints ground items per tile, asking 'what items would the GUI DISPLAY on this tile for the avatar' (the visible/remembered view), not 'what items physically exist in raw world state'.
scope: The display-filtered, seen/visibility-gated view of each tile's ground-item stack as the GUI would paint it (only tiles the avatar can currently see or remembers), not the raw stack of every tile in radius.
decisive_source: src/arcopolis_export.cpp::write_entities(items) — iterates points_in_radius and writes get_map().i_at(p) for every in-window tile directly, with no seen/visibility filter, so it emits raw map ground-stack state rather than the displayed view.
divergence: A tile inside the export window that the avatar cannot currently see (behind a wall / never explored) holding a dropped item: raw i_at reports the item so the frontend paints it, but the GUI would draw nothing there since it isn't seen/remembered — exposing S-state leaking as display.
